claims.title: Landing-bucket extracts may be readable on the scheduler read path
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` remains unverified on `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files`, an attacker able to observe the landing-network path can intercept the partner extract files read by `process:ingest-scheduler` from `store:landing-bucket`. Those files contain health-related claim records with member names and dates of birth. The disclosure also gives the observer the input subsequently processed by `process:spark-transform-job`; this draft is conditional on the transport-encryption unknown, not an assertion that the object-storage API is plaintext.

quotes.text: The extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files` has unverified transport encryption but an attacker must first obtain an on-path position within `boundary:landing-network`. Impact is high because `store:landing-bucket` holds `pii` and `health` extracts containing member names and dates of birth.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require encrypted object-store reads
mitigations.detail: Set and enforce TLS for `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files`, validating the storage endpoint certificate; use workload identity or mTLS where supported.

mitigations.summary: Minimize exposed extract contents
mitigations.detail: Avoid placing direct member identifiers in paths and object names, and restrict scheduler reads to the partner folder and objects required for each run.

claims.title: Scheduler-to-metadata-database traffic may expose SFTP keys and connection strings
claims.description: If transport protection is absent on `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections`, an attacker observing that connection can intercept the connection strings and partner SFTP keys retrieved by `process:ingest-scheduler` from `store:airflow-metadata-database`. Holding a partner key enables subsequent access to the partner-upload interface on `flow:entity:insurance-partner>store:landing-bucket>push-daily-extract`; the disclosure is conditional because both the protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unstated.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional: the protocol and transport protection on `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections` are unknown, and an attacker still needs a landing-network observation point. Impact is high because `store:airflow-metadata-database` holds `credentials` and `secrets`, including partner SFTP keys.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate metadata-database connections
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with authenticated endpoints for `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections` and record the selected protocol and cipher policy in the model.

mitigations.summary: Move partner keys into a dedicated secret manager
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived, per-partner credentials retrieved over an authenticated secret-manager channel instead of exposing static SFTP keys through ordinary Airflow metadata reads.

claims.title: Claim records may be readable while loaded into the warehouse
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:spark-transform-job>store:claims-warehouse>load-records`, an attacker with a position on the warehouse-network path can intercept normalized claim records while `process:spark-transform-job` writes them to `store:claims-warehouse`. The captured records include the health and personal data later made available to warehouse queries; this is conditional on the unstated transport control rather than a claim that the BigQuery API is unencrypted.

quotes.text: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the transport control on `flow:process:spark-transform-job>store:claims-warehouse>load-records` is unknown and the attacker needs a warehouse-network observation point. Impact is high because `store:claims-warehouse` is confidential and tagged `pii` and `health`.

mitigations.summary: Require TLS for warehouse loads
mitigations.detail: Configure and verify TLS for `flow:process:spark-transform-job>store:claims-warehouse>load-records`, including certificate validation and a service identity scoped to the load operation.

mitigations.summary: Reduce raw personal data on ingestion paths
mitigations.detail: Tokenize or encrypt the most sensitive member-identifying fields before the transform sends rows to the warehouse where operationally feasible.

claims.title: Analyst warehouse queries may be observable in transit
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries`, a warehouse-network attacker able to observe that connection can intercept query results containing claim records and member identifiers returned to `entity:data-analyst`. This reveals the same confidential health and PII data that the dataset-wide analyst grant makes queryable; the disclosure is conditional on the unstated encryption attribute.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries` has unverified transport encryption and the attacker needs an on-path foothold in `boundary:warehouse-network`. Impact is high because the queried warehouse is confidential and holds member-identifying `pii` and `health` records.

mitigations.summary: Enforce encrypted analyst-to-warehouse sessions
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with certificate validation for `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries` and prevent clients from falling back to unencrypted connections.

mitigations.summary: Restrict result exposure
mitigations.detail: Use views that return only the fields required for an analyst's task, so intercepted result sets contain less direct identifying data.

claims.title: A landing-bucket storage copy may disclose partner health extracts
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` is confidential and holds PII and health extracts, but `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker obtaining a storage-layer copy of the bucket—such as operational media, an export, or a snapshot—can read the extracts without authenticating through the SFTP front end or `process:ingest-scheduler`. The extracts can then be correlated with the normalized records loaded downstream into `store:claims-warehouse`; this is explicitly conditional on the unresolved at-rest posture.

quotes.text:
I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted or whether the Airflow
metadata database is encrypted at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:landing-bucket` has no verified at-rest encryption and storage copies can bypass the application path, although the control may be present. Impact is high because the confidential store holds `pii` and `health` claim records with member names and dates of birth.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the landing bucket and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Verify the current setting, then require managed-key encryption at rest for `store:landing-bucket`, including backups, exports, snapshots, and replicated objects.

mitigations.summary: Constrain storage-layer access
mitigations.detail: Limit export, snapshot, key-use, and storage-administration roles to separate least-privilege principals and audit bulk object reads.

claims.title: An unencrypted metadata-database copy may reveal partner access keys
claims.description: `store:airflow-metadata-database` stores connection strings and partner SFTP keys and is classified confidential, while its `encryption_at_rest` setting is unknown. If it is unencrypted at rest, an attacker holding a database backup, snapshot, or other storage copy can recover those credentials without using `process:ingest-scheduler`. The recovered partner keys can then be used against the SFTP upload interface feeding `store:landing-bucket`; this is a conditional storage-copy disclosure, not an assertion that encryption is absent.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:airflow-metadata-database` has unverified encryption at rest and a storage copy bypasses its normal read path. Impact is high because the store contains `credentials` and `secrets`, and the partner static key is stated not to be rotated.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt metadata storage and its copies with controlled keys
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for `store:airflow-metadata-database`, including backups and snapshots, with KMS permissions separated from database administration.

mitigations.summary: Eliminate long-lived partner keys from metadata
mitigations.detail: Store partner credentials in a dedicated secret manager, issue distinct short-lived credentials where supported, and rotate the existing static keys immediately.

claims.title: A claims-warehouse storage copy may expose the health-record corpus
claims.description: `store:claims-warehouse` is a confidential BigQuery dataset containing normalized claim records with member names and dates of birth, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If storage encryption is not enabled, anyone obtaining an operational copy of the warehouse data can read the corpus outside the SSO query path. The result is full-dataset disclosure of the information otherwise consumed by `entity:data-analyst`; this draft remains conditional until the at-rest control is verified.

quotes.text: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:claims-warehouse` has no verified at-rest encryption and a snapshot or exported copy does not require a live SSO session. Impact is high because the confidential warehouse is tagged `pii` and `health` and contains normalized records for all partner extracts.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce warehouse encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Confirm the at-rest posture of `store:claims-warehouse`, enforce managed-key encryption for the dataset and every export, backup, snapshot, and replica, and restrict key use.

mitigations.summary: Protect exports as strictly as the dataset
mitigations.detail: Require explicit approval, logging, expiry, and least-privilege access for warehouse extracts so an operational copy cannot become a lower-control disclosure path.

claims.title: Code in the scheduler can read every landed partner extract
claims.description: `process:ingest-scheduler` lists `store:landing-bucket` and reads whatever files are present. An attacker who gains code execution in the scheduler inherits this read path and can read the PII and health extracts across partner folders rather than only a single expected file. The copied records become the input for downstream normalization by `process:spark-transform-job` and can be correlated with the warehouse corpus. This is distinct from interception or storage-copy exposure: it uses the scheduler's authorized live access.

quotes.text:
An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists
the bucket, and reads whatever is there.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first execute code in `process:ingest-scheduler`; its exposure is unknown rather than internet-facing. Impact is high because the scheduler reads every file in `store:landing-bucket`, which holds confidential `pii` and `health` extracts.

mitigations.summary: Scope the scheduler to expected partner objects
mitigations.detail: Give `process:ingest-scheduler` a narrowly scoped identity that can read only the expected partner folder and object manifest for each run.

mitigations.summary: Isolate and monitor scheduler execution
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated workload identity, restrict scheduler egress to required services, and alert on bulk or cross-partner object reads outside the nightly job manifest.

claims.title: Code in the scheduler can recover unrotated partner SFTP keys
claims.description: `process:ingest-scheduler` reads connection strings and partner SFTP keys from `store:airflow-metadata-database`. An attacker who executes code in the scheduler can recover those credentials through the service's normal database access. The partner static keys have not been rotated, so each recovered key remains a standing credential that can reach the SFTP upload path to `store:landing-bucket`; this is credential disclosure through an authorized reader, not a claim about encryption at rest.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
Each partner has a static key we issued when they onboarded; the keys have not changed since.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker first needs code execution in `process:ingest-scheduler`, whose exposure is unknown. Impact is high because `store:airflow-metadata-database` holds `credentials` and `secrets`, and the disclosed partner static keys are stated not to be rotated.

mitigations.summary: Use a dedicated secret manager and workload-scoped access
mitigations.detail: Remove partner SFTP keys from `store:airflow-metadata-database`; allow the scheduler to retrieve only the credential needed for a specific partner run from a secret manager.

mitigations.summary: Rotate and replace static partner keys
mitigations.detail: Immediately rotate all existing partner keys and migrate to distinct short-lived or certificate-based partner credentials with revocation capability.

claims.title: A dataset-wide analyst grant exposes member-identifying claim data
claims.description: An honest-but-curious or compromised `entity:data-analyst` authenticated through SSO can use `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries` to query the whole `store:claims-warehouse`, including member-identifying columns, because the grant is dataset-wide. This lets a legitimate principal retrieve health and PII records beyond a task requiring de-identified analysis. The resulting corpus can be exported or correlated with other information outside the warehouse; the disclosure is caused by the grant's scope, not by a failure to authenticate.

quotes.text:
They are on the warehouse network and
authenticate with SSO, but the grant is dataset-wide — we have not split
member-identifying columns out.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because analysts already authenticate with SSO and have a stated dataset-wide query grant on `store:claims-warehouse`. Impact is high because the confidential warehouse contains member-identifying `pii` and `health` claim records, and the grant permits corpus-scale querying.

mitigations.summary: Replace dataset-wide access with least-privilege views
mitigations.detail: Create role-specific views or authorized datasets that omit member-identifying columns by default, and grant `entity:data-analyst` only the views required for approved analysis.

mitigations.summary: Add query-level controls and detection
mitigations.detail: Apply column-level policy tags, row filters, approval for re-identification access, and alerts for broad extracts or enumeration-shaped queries.
